in1.text: This is Trip Risk Checker. Before you book, it tells you the chance that a flight gets you to your meeting an hour late, from a full year of US flights.

ck1.text: Start on Check a trip. First, choose where you fly from.

ck2.text: Then where you need to be. Any US airport works, not only the ones with a nonstop flight.

ck3.text: Pick your travel date. The day of the week and the month both change the risk.

ck5.text: Every nonstop and same-airline connection is ranked by the chance of arriving an hour late, with the route, the total time and the cancellation rate.

ck6.text: The verdict tells you what to book, and how many points safer it is.

ck7.text: Further down: the same route by departure time, and the weather you can expect at both airports in that month.

ck8.text: And whether a stop is worth it: the extra risk, the extra hours, and the fare saving you would need to break even.

co1.text: The second page puts a price on that risk.

co2.text: Set three numbers: what the meeting is worth, what an hour of your time is worth, and what a night stranded costs.

co4.text: You get the expected cost of the recommended flight, of the riskiest option, and the gap between them: the most a safer fare is worth paying.

co5.text: Below, what each booking habit costs per trip.

hb1.text: The third page ranks twenty connecting hubs by what happens to one-stop trips through them.

hb2.text: The best and the riskiest hub, then the full table.

hb3.text: The map covers every large and medium airport: disruption rate, adverse-weather days for any month, or winter fragility.

hb4.text: Dot size is departures. Hover any airport for its details.

ou1.text: Know the risk before you book. Trip Risk Checker, at trip-risk-checker dot vercel dot app.
